title: PYTHIA: Universal Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: KGQA systems must answer user questions over knowledge graphs despite challenges involving training-data coverage, KG-specific constraints, ontology updates, complex exploration, performance degradation, and response latency.

gap.claim: Existing KGQA approaches trade off accuracy, responsiveness, versatility, adaptability to ontology updates, training requirements, and predictable performance.

contributions.claim: PYTHIA is a training-free, plug-and-play solution for KGQA over any RDF knowledge graph.
PYTHIA uses an LLM agent guided by a relation-centric conceptual model and a tool suite for entity linking, graph exploration, and query execution.
PYTHIA separates agent responsibilities for interpreting intent, orchestrating tool calls, and evaluating outputs from tool interfaces that abstract complex processes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors evaluate PYTHIA and prior systems across four knowledge graphs and six datasets.
The authors report a median performance improvement of 15.31% and improved cost and time efficiency at the performance frontier.

narrative_sequence.summary: KGQA answers questions using data retrieved from knowledge graphs.
Existing supervised, KG-specific, and training-free approaches face trade-offs involving data requirements, versatility, ontology changes, complexity, performance, and latency.
The paper presents PYTHIA as a training-free, plug-and-play RDF-KGQA solution built around an LLM agent, a conceptual model, and specialized tools.
The authors assess PYTHIA and prior systems across four knowledge graphs and six datasets.
The authors report a 15.31% median performance improvement with better cost and time efficiency at the performance frontier.

source_observation.claim: A tool-using LLM agent can coordinate entity linking, graph exploration, and query execution through simple interfaces.

interpretation.claim: Separating intent reasoning and orchestration from complex tool internals may reduce the reasoning burden on an agent.

application.claim: For heterogeneous knowledge-graph applications, consider a KG-agnostic agent architecture with specialized tools and explicit task guidance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how this architecture performs across other domains, graph formats, or workloads beyond the reported evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated knowledge graphs, datasets, baselines, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide absolute performance values or details of the cost and time measurements.
The abstract does not describe limitations, failure cases, or implementation details.
